title: Egress backpressure sanitizer and tiered shedding patch
author: Maya Ortiz
description: Motivation: Recent incidents showed intermittent egress saturation from regional edge clusters to downstream third-party egress endpoints (NAT/gateway rate limits) caused tail latency spikes and cascading request failures for low-priority tenants. This PR introduces an 'egress backpressure sanitizer' that enforces a soft, per-region egress budget and a tiered shedding strategy to gracefully degrade non-critical workloads before failing production-critical paths. Summary of changes: 1) runtime/egress/sanitizer: new egress_budget controller that tracks per-region token and connection egress over rolling windows and exposes a simple API (Allow/Defer/Reject) used by the request router. 2) routing/policy: tiered_shed policy that maps tenant priority and route tags to a staged degradation pipeline (stage 0: no-op, stage 1: reduce reranker/recall timeouts and enable cached-prefix fast-paths, stage 2: strip expensive embeddings and fall back to low-cost model variants, stage 3: hard reject low-priority requests). 3) observability: metrics and traces (egress_budget.used, egress_budget.limit, egress_shed.stage, tenant_shed.event) and a dashboard snapshot for incident review. 4) defaults and rollout: conservative default budgets per region with a canary gating config that gradually expands from 5% to 100% of traffic over three hours. Backward compatibility: policy defaults are conservative and off by default for dedicated/private installs; hosted will enable the small budget in pilot regions only. Checklist: - [x] Design doc reviewed (ENG-8421) - [x] Unit tests for sanitizer controller - [x] Integration tests for staged_shed policy with local e2e harness - [x] Load tests (5x production) in perf-canary cluster - [x] Canary rollout plan + rollback playbook attached Changesets: small API surface; no public SDK changes. Testing and validation: synthetic load tests recreated egress saturation conditions and validated that stage transitions blocked low-priority work while preserving 99th percentile for top-tier tenants. Metrics show a 82% reduction in customer-visible 5xxs to third-party egress during the synthetic bursts. Rollout: feature-gated behind runtime.feature.egress_sanitizer; canary config targets region us-west-2, tenant cohorts: internal-testers->10%, beta-customers->25%, then ramp. Implementation notes: the sanitizer keeps a compact token-bucket-like state keyed by (region, tenant_cohort) and evicts stale entries after two roll windows; it marshals decisions into request metadata for downstream observability. Performance: microbenchmarks show <150ns additional median latency on the critical hot path and negligible memory overhead. Related work: implements recommendations from postmortem SUP-1219 and complements earlier SLO relaxation primitives (ENG-8425). Merge rationale: hotpatch to avoid repeat outages during peak third-party egress events. Rollback plan: revert feature flag and a follow-up patch to remove the routing hook if needed.
commits: Add egress_budget controller and basic unit tests
Implement tiered_shed policy and integrate with router
Add metrics, dashboard snapshots, and canary config
Fix race on sanitizer eviction and add backfill for legacy entries
review_conversation: Liam Chen: This looks good overall but can we replace the hard-coded 2-window eviction with a config knob? Author: Added runtime.config.egress.eviction_windows and defaulted to 2 in main config.
Priya Nair: Would prefer the stage transitions to have hysteresis to avoid flapping. Author: Implemented a simple cooldown per key (30s) and documented it in the design notes.
Carlos Mendes: CI flake on the e2e harness, re-ran tests after fixing timing. Author: Added a deterministic seed to the harness, CI green.
SRE: Please confirm there is an alerting path for excessive rejections. Author: Added tenant_shed.event counter and a PagerDuty rule for >1% sustained rejections for top-tier cohorts.
release_notes: Introduced an egress backpressure sanitizer and tiered shedding policy to prevent third-party egress saturation from causing service-wide failures. Feature is feature-flagged and rolled out via canary. Operators should review new egress_sanitizer dashboard and update eviction/budget defaults if they operate in constrained egress environments.
notes_for_ops: Feature flag: runtime.feature.egress_sanitizer. Canary config located at deploy/canaries/egress_sanitizer_canary.yaml. Key metrics: egress_budget.used, egress_budget.limit, egress_shed.stage, tenant_shed.event. Rollback: flip feature flag to false and restart router processes in affected region.
